summary: Five working documents plus one script describe the Regime-Direction Law project at three successive moments, and they have drifted apart. glunet_modeling.md (Jun 9, 21:26) establishes the precursor problem: adding GLU-Net to the shared 3-architecture ridge diluted the pooled motion headline from 0.51/0.45/0.32 to 0.31/0.36/0.18 (LOTO/LOBO/JOINT) and hurt CATs++/RAFT per-variant numbers; its Section 9 resolution is a two-pool fit (CATs+++RAFT pooled reproduces 0.52/0.46/0.31; GLU-Net fit separately) with consensus fraction 0.63/0.71/0.39 of the 0.731 ceiling, and it explicitly retracts an earlier "0.619 to 0.731 ceiling" comparison as confounded. REGIME_DIRECTION_FINDING.md (Jun 9, 23:15) supersedes the two-pool framing with the law itself: scratch models are precision-bound (train-to-target distance predicts transfer), pretrained models recall-bound (target-to-train); a fit-free one-bit regime rule scores +0.498 mean within-context Spearman, essentially at the inter-variant ceiling (+0.528, fraction ~0.99), beating every fitted pooling structure; it documents an adversarial verification (flip +0.818, exact permutation p=0.0286), a passed pre-registered out-of-sample FF-arm test on the kubric intervention grid (precision +0.621 vs recall -0.125 vs sym +0.096), a DINO negative control (no flip, p=0.54), and rule-based consensus 0.79/0.80/0.81 of 0.731. RESULTS_TABLES.md (Jun 9, 23:43) consolidates these into tables T1-T9, opening with "Every number below is on disk now; nothing pending" -- a claim that is no longer true. HANDOFF_tt_grid_parity.md (Jun 10, 13:18) diagnoses why the OOS pretrained (TT) arm had only 3 sources vs FF's 10 (un-harvested old snapshots) and prescribes 6 harvests + 1 verify + 1 retrain plus removal of a hardcoded trial19 96.1158 line in blocks.py. run_clean_pipeline.sh regenerates the now-superseded shared-ridge v4 results and still fits a middlebury predictor; score_synthetic_fractal.py rescores the trial76 FF cell on four benchmarks including middlebury. Cross-checking disk state reveals the handoff WAS executed on Jun 10 (4 symlinks at 13:21, lowtex_matte and trial76 TT trained 13:28, trial19 TT retrained 18:09, hardcode removed), and two downstream regenerations occurred that neither finding doc reflects: (1) the verification REPORT.md was re-run Jun 10 12:47 with Middlebury excluded (891 rows, 9 benchmarks), shifting every per-variant rho (flip statistic now +0.899, not +0.818; catspp F/F precision +0.527 not +0.558/+0.600; glunet T/T recall +0.763 not +0.734/+0.719; RAFT d +0.098 not +0.22) -- so THREE versions of the law's headline table coexist; (2) intervention_oos.csv was regenerated Jun 10 21:11 without middlebury and with the TT arm at n=9, and the new TT-arm correlations show precision GREATER than recall on all three benchmarks (flyingthings 0.733 vs 0.083; kitti2012 0.800 vs 0.650; kitti2015 0.383 vs -0.100) -- the face-value OPPOSITE of the law's pretrained-recall prediction, recorded nowhere in any document. The FF-arm PASS survives Middlebury removal (its three remaining per-benchmark values match T7 exactly). trial19's TT retrain peaks at 96.37 K2015, rank 4/10 in the TT arm -- consistent with the handoff's "mid-pack" prediction but making the documented "rank 2/4" and the hardcoded 96.1158 stale.
